description: Localized command-list text: character descriptions, passive/attack names, and long attack descriptions. CommandList rows reference these strings by id; the command-list widgets resolve and specially parse the description text.

ID.simple: Command-list text id (row key), e.g. CMD_CHARACTER_DESCRIPTION_CP_010.
ID.technical: FName ID in FGameDataTableRow_GameText, identical to the row name used by FindRow. The owning CommandList row stores these ids in many named FName/FName-array fields (Id_CommandListText_CharacterDescription, Id_CommandListText_PassiveName/Description[], Id_CommandListText_NormalAttack_*_Name/Description, cursed-energy/extra/super variants). UGameCommandListWidget checks IsNone() to show/hide an entry and copies the ids into FGameCommandListActionParameter for the action widget; name ids are applied directly with SetTextIdOnly, description ids are fetched with GetText. The table is loaded as CommandListTextDataTable_<Language> in slot 4 of the GameText array.

Text.simple: The localized command-list name or description body.
Text.technical: FString row text (+0x10), resolved by GetText/GetGameText and run through FormatText ( from the glossary map, from request parameters, modifiers). Description rows have an application-level mini-language in addition: UGameCommandListActionWidget splits them on the literal '', then on '【'/'[' or ':'/line breaks to build explanation frames; '' markup is parsed by the rich-text widget. Name rows are short labels without that split. Empty ids disable the corresponding UI entry; an existing row with an empty string renders empty. The En export contains 628 rows (one empty) with 51 GLO tags; no DYN tags in this group.

notes: Same FGameDataTableRow_GameText struct and 11 identical language variants as other GameText tables (628 ids each in the companion export). Slot 4 of the 14-table search array; Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 assigns each language variant to a cooked chunk.

Cross-table join: CommandListDataTable supplies the ids, this table supplies the strings; glossary ids inside the text are resolved from GlossaryTextDataTable_<Language>, so a CMD row can embed a GLS_ term.

The '<SplitCommand>' token and full-width bracket parsing are consumer-side conventions specific to command descriptions; the data table itself stores them as ordinary characters in the FString. No prefix-specific table lookup is used, so colliding ids in earlier tables take precedence.

Reconstruction caveat: GetText/GetGameText/FormatText are byte-matched; FindTextRow/Tick are behaviour-certified (status/functions.json 0x14af290, 0x14c96f0; BG03). Only partial Content is available; no claims about retail Blueprint-only presentation code.

usages.detail: Sets the character explanation text block to Id_CommandListText_CharacterDescription.
Bounds-checks the passive name/description id arrays and builds passive action parameters.
Copies normal-attack name and description ids into FGameCommandListActionParameter and tests the name id for visibility.
Fetches the description string with GetText and parses its <SplitCommand> sections into explanation frames.
Loads CommandListTextDataTable_<Language> into the shared GameText table list.
